newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba harvest begins, fusarium damage cited.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba harvest begins, fusarium damage cited.

text.p: Sunny, warm weather allowed harvest to begin across Manitoba with the extent of fusarium damage yet to be determined, Manitoba Agriculture's report for the week ended August 26 said.
Southwest Manitoba - Harvesting of cereals began in most districts and should be general this week. Most harvested wheat so far graded number one with moderate to high protein.
Swathing of canola was underway in all districts. The level of fusarium infestation has yet to be determined.
Northwest Manitoba - Five percent of wheat and barley crops were swathed while swathing just began in canola.
Some field peas were harvested with early yield indications as high as 45 bushels an acre. Some oats were cut for feed and yields were rated as good.

Central Manitoba - About 25 percent of cereals were swathed with five percent combined. Wheat yields in the Pilot Mound, Somerset and Treherne districts were average to above average with most wheat grading number two with protein at 12 to 15 percent.
Other districts began swathing with yields expected to be slightly below average due to disease. Fall rye harvest was near complete, yields averaged 60 to 85 bushels per acre.

Eastern Manitoba - St. Pierre and Dugald saw 1.5 to two inches of rain last week. Swathing began and should be general by the end of the week. Fusarium and septoria were common in wheat but yields were expected to be average. Aphids were reported in flax around St. Pierre.
Interlake region - Two inches of rain slowed harvest but five to 10 percent of barley and wheat were swathed and swathing began in canola.
